content.thinking:
I'm planning the chopper's design in one pass without testing first—long fork, Overwatch-style bold shapes, dark gunmetal and white body with an orange accent and small glow lights—then starting on the root skeleton structure.

Working out the joint hierarchy (frame, steering fork, front/rear wheels, swingarm, kickstand, handlebars) with precise coordinates for the raked front fork and wide tires, then beginning the wheel geometry with torus shapes...

Still writing helper functions...

Setting up the color palette with graphite, orange accent, white, chrome, black, rubber, and leather tones for the model.

For the tank, I'm writing a paint function that creates a white racing stripe down the center with dark pinstripe edges against an orange base, keeping it simple with a teardrop shape.

I'm building the tank as a loft across four stations tapering from the seat down to a pointed nose, bound to the body bone, then planning the V-twin engine with an angled crankcase and finned cylinders.

Working out the cylinder tilt geometry, I'm rotating about the X axis so the front cylinder leans forward +35° and the rear leans back -35° from a shared crank base position, placing each cylinder's center offset along its tilted axis, with fins modeled as separate stacked parts along each cylinder.

Now I'm laying out the frame tubes -- top tube from head to seat post, down tube from head to crank, and a double-cradle structure with symmetric rods running from the frame down to the swing pivot and seat area on both sides.

Next I'm working out the head tube and fork geometry, computing the steering axis direction, positioning the triple clamp, and deriving the fork stanchion offsets from the axle position along the fork direction vector.

Still working out positions...

Still building wheel geometry...

Front wheel at radius .32 with similar torus proportions. I'll use a low-poly torus (8 radial, 24 tubular segments) and add a tread pattern by painting alternating rubber shades based on the UV bands around the tube, giving a simple segmented tire look.

Now I'm shaping the seat with lofted leather stations along the body, then planning the rear fender as a swept bezier arc above the rear wheel.

Adding exhaust pipes next, chrome drag pipes sweeping from the cylinders back along the right side with heat-tinted color bands and a shorter secondary pipe on the left.

Now I'm positioning foot pegs and forward controls for a chopper-style stance, with a platform and rod geometry placed low and forward, plus a kickstand hinge joint with its rod angled down and back from the frame.

Deciding to keep the kickstand folded up against the body since the tires already rest on the ground, so I'm placing the rod and foot pad in a stowed horizontal position rather than deployed.

Now I'm adding the chain/belt drive connecting the crank sprocket to the rear sprocket, including a belt guard slab piece.

Actually I'll add real rear shocks connecting the swingarm to the frame, with a dark rod for the shock body and an accent-colored spring cylinder, bone-weighted lower to the swing and upper to the body.

Now I'm shaping the swingarm itself with a boxy rod from pivot to axle, plus a cylindrical hub for the axle. For the engine, I'm placing a chrome air cleaner cylinder on the left side near the front of the tank, oriented along the x-axis with an accent cap.

I'm also adding an oil tank box behind the engine, and planning decals for the tank sides -- a mirrored hexagon-and-lightning-bolt emblem rendered as an SVG texture applied via decal onto the lofted tank surface.

I'm skipping text decals to avoid font issues, opting for simple shapes instead, plus a plain number plate decal on the rear fender. For the frame I'm going with dark graphite with orange accent cuts, and considering adding a thin cyan glow tube beneath the engine for underglow lighting.

Actually I'll simplify to one accent color -- orange -- rather than mixing orange and cyan, keeping the Overwatch-style single accent tech look with warm headlight and rim glow tones. Now I'm sketching the chrome sissy bar and backrest sweep geometry.

Adding fork gaiter rib details and the lower slider tube...

Now I'm shaping the front fender as a curved arc sweeping over the wheel, defining angle ranges from the back-top toward the front, with a boxed cross-section that tapers slightly and carries an orange accent color, possibly with a white stripe detail.

I'm also adding the front brake disc as a thin dark chrome cylinder mounted at the wheel hub, and positioning a caliper box just behind the axle on the fork slider.

Now I'm working on the headlight: adding small bracket rods connecting the fork legs to the headlight sides, placing the headlight body as a scaled sphere forward of the steering axis, and layering a lens circle with a glow ring facing forward.

Checking clearances—the headlight sits above and clear of the front fender's extent, and the front wheel bone stays properly childed to the steering axis. Estimating around 250 total parts, with overall length near 2.6m and a 1.95m wheelbase, which feels proportionate for a realistic chopper build.

Now I'm verifying torus geometry for the tires: with 24 tubular and 8 radial segments, a vertex falls exactly at the bottom of the tube, so the wheel's lowest point sits cleanly at the expected radius without gaps. I'm confirming the torus orientation—rotating it to lie flat in the right plane so it reads correctly as a wheel.

I'm sketching out the joint structure: spokes and hub sit in the YZ plane, the root frame joint anchors the whole assembly, and each wheel joint uses a hinge role with the appropriate axis direction. I'm placing the kickstand joint near the rear-bottom of the frame with a tilted hinge direction so it can fold in and out naturally, and deciding to skip extra details like a throttle or chain for now to keep the model focused.

Setting up the geometry helpers and type definitions for the build...

Writing geometry helpers...

Still designing the triple clamp geometry... now moving to the engine block, planning the crankcase box, round side covers with chrome accents, and angled cylinder placement for the V-twin layout.

Working out the exhaust pipe path for the front cylinder, tracing coordinates from the head down and back with a tapering radius, checking it clears the rear cylinder's backward tilt.

I'm also checking for collisions between all these components: the exhaust pipe versus the transmission box, the drive belt, footpegs, and swingarm, then noticing the swingarm and sprocket overlap at x=.15 and adjusting the swingarm position outward to x=.17 to resolve it.

Still adjusting for collisions, I'm repositioning the pipe to x=.27 and the swingarm to x=.15, but that now puts the footpegs in the pipe's path, so I'm thinking about shifting the foot controls forward along z to clear the exhaust route near the fork.

I'll place a dark rubber footboard as a small box, then rework the exhaust pipe's path coordinates so it curves down and back without clipping the frame, and tighten the belt and pulleys closer to the transmission at x=.12 so they hug properly. I'm skipping a separate belt cover and considering whether the frame tubes should stay dark or become an accent color.

Now I'm positioning the frame rods in dark graphite, routing the top tube under the tank, the down tube from the head to mid-frame, and the cradle/seat tube/rail curves using swept catmull paths, making sure every piece is assigned to the frame bone -- then checking how the tank sits relative to the engine's front cylinder head height.

Moving on to seat placement, I'm adjusting the seat stations further back in z so they don't overlap the tank's rear edge, shifting them to roughly -0.3 to -0.85 while keeping the height centered around the rails. I'm then tracing the fender's curve from behind the seat down toward the rear wheel, and positioning the rear wheel's center and outer radius to line up with everything else.

Checking the fender clearance against the wheel at a few z positions to make sure it doesn't clip the tire, and adjusting one fender point to keep a small gap. Then I'm placing the taillight just past the end of the fender, and figuring out where the license plate sits so it clears the rear wheel but stays close to the fender end.

Now I'm setting up the plate as a textured plane facing backward with a dark backing box behind it, plus a separate decal on the tank using a bolt-style texture, making sure the sweep surface accepts the decal orientation correctly.

Checking tank geometry to position the decal reasonably on its surface, then designing the tank paint pattern: a thin white stripe down the center and darker graphite coloring on the lower sides, based on the tank's vertical span.

Still working out positioning for the chrome fuel cap near the top of the tank and the handlebar riser location at the head tube.

Still working out mirror and handlebar geometry...

Defining the wheel assembly...

Working out the specific radii for front and rear wheels, confirming tire thickness matches the outer/inner radius math, then setting up torus geometry parameters before moving to the spoke generation loop.

Still writing spoke placement...

Now adding the rear sprocket as a toothed cylinder with an accent ring, and planning an underglow strip beneath the engine using a glowing orange rod segment.

I'm layering in rider ergonomics and small hardware details: footpegs, shifter, brake pedal, oil tank, battery, heat shields, and bolt rings around each engine cover using small chrome sphere clusters. I'll also add fork bolts, decal strips, and a tank emblem, then finalize the metadata object and return the completed root structure.

Now I'm nailing down the full color palette (orange, chrome, graphite, frame steel, glow tones, brass, dark blacks) and sketching an SVG bolt/emblem shape—a chevron-style shield with a dark outline for the tank badge.

Writing SVG emblem shape...

Then I'll move to the license plate SVG with white base, orange border, and bar glyphs, plus a typed helper function for building geometry parts with explicit rotation vector types.

Adding heat shield geometry...

I'm working out the fender's front strut geometry, connecting the slider to a hung point ahead of the fork, then positioning the front brake rotor near the hub.

I move the rotor outward slightly so it clears the tire edge, checking its radius fits inside the tire's inner diameter, and decide to skip adding a rear rotor for simplicity. Then I verify the rear tire, sprocket, and swingarm widths don't overlap, confirm the seat and sissy bar placement look right, and do a final pass checking TypeScript types and unused variables before finalizing the code.

Writing bolt ring positions for the covers...

Now placing the crank, transmission box, and air cleaner assembly, checking they don't overlap with the exhaust and front cylinder, plus the carb rod connecting the cleaner to the head. That should finish the layout, ready to write it all out.
